subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@finsecure.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated vs Private VPC - recap & next steps

Hi Alex - thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Key takeaways:
- Primary requirement: strict data isolation (no mixing with other customers) and customer-managed encryption keys for model inputs/outputs and logs.
- Residency: data must remain in your AWS account/region.
- Auditability: longer retention of audit logs (3+ years) and access to the audit trail for compliance reviews.
- Volume/throughput: ~500 concurrent inference requests at peak, ~2M tokens/day (approx).

How Redwood options map to your needs:
- Hosted API: not recommended for this use-case - control plane and logs are shared.
- Dedicated: single-tenant GPU pools for inference (isolated runtime), optional VPC peering for egress control. Control plane remains Redwood-managed; by default observability and logs are stored in Redwood's systems but can be configured to forward logs. BYOK support is available for encrypted artifacts (optional).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full private control plane deployed into your VPC or on-prem environment, customer-managed KMS/HSM, full audit log ownership, and no Redwood-managed logs retained by default. This provides the strongest isolation and is our typical recommendation for regulated financial workloads.

Open questions for you (to confirm next step):
1) Is customer-managed KMS mandatory, or is BYOK sufficient?
2) Do you need Private deployment inside a specific AWS account (we can do VPC AMI/CloudFormation) or an on-prem package?
3) Any additional compliance needs (PCI scope, specific certs) beyond SOC 2?

Attachments: SOC2-report-2025.pdf (summary), redwood_private_deployment_diagram.png, dedicated-vs-vpc-matrix.pdf

Proposed next steps:
- Quick technical deep-dive (30m) with Mateo + Rachel to walk through KMS/HSM integration and log flows.
- Security questionnaire & evidence handoff.
- High-level TCO delta (Dedicated vs Private) and timeline (Private typically 6-8 weeks for first install + security review; Dedicated can be weeks for reserved capacity).

Which day/time works for your security/infra folks this week? Thanks - looking forward to continuing.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@finsecure.com>

Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated vs Private VPC - recap & next steps

Hi Marissa - really helpful summary, thanks. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We process transaction metadata and some tokenized payment references (we do not store raw PANs). Our security/compliance team is insisting on customer-managed keys + assurance that logs and model caches are never accessible to other tenants.
- Residency: must be in our AWS account in us-west-2.
- Log retention: 3 years minimum and ability to produce audit logs on demand.

Questions: 
1) For Dedicated - can you confirm whether any model KV-cache or temporary artifacts are written outside the dedicated pool (i.e., any shared storage)? We need guarantees around data not being replicated to shared services.
2) For Private - what's the typical SLA for updates/patching and how are security patches handled? We want minimal downtime and a clear maintenance window policy.
3) Cost delta: can you provide a ballpark monthly delta for Dedicated reserved capacity vs a Private VPC deployment (initial sizing: 2 x A100-equivalent for current workload)?

Sarah from procurement is looped for timelines and budget. We're aiming to have a security review by next Tuesday. Can Mateo or Rachel be available for a 30m session tomorrow or Monday?

Thanks,
Alex
Director, Infrastructure Security | FinSecure
alex.taylor@finsecure.com
+1 (206) 555-0189

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@finsecure.com>
Cc: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@finsecure.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated vs Private VPC - recap & next steps

Thanks Alex - answers inline below.

1) Dedicated isolation model: the inference runtime (GPU pools) is single-tenant and does not co-locate customer inference processes with other customers. However, the Redwood control plane and certain meta-services (scheduling, billing, model registry) remain managed by Redwood. We do not write KV-cache or model inputs to any cross-tenant storage; runtime caches stay on the provisioned instances. For absolute assurance (no Redwood-managed control plane access to logs/model artifacts), Private VPC is the recommended approach.

2) Private update/patching: we operate a managed private control plane with a clear maintenance and patch policy. Patches are staged in our canary environments, validated with your security team, and we schedule maintenance windows with you. SLA for Private deployments is negotiated (we offer enterprise SLAs for Private customers).

3) Cost delta (ballpark): Dedicated reserved capacity (2 x A100-equivalent) - ~$55k-$70k/month (committed pricing). Private VPC initial delivery has a one-time platform deployment fee (~$120k-$180k) + ongoing managed service (~$35k-$50k/month) depending on support and retention options. I'll get a formal quote from finance but wanted to give an initial sense.

Next steps:
- Mateo and Rachel are available Mon 2026-07-06 10:00-11:30 PT or Tue 2026-07-07 09:00-12:00 PT for a security/architecture deep-dive. Please confirm which time works.
- We'll also share the detailed BYOK/KMS integration guide and a control-plane access model for Private.

Attached: dedicated-vs-vpc-matrix.pdf (detailed comparison)

Best,
Marissa

- Estimated delivery timeline: assuming FinSecure signs the PoC/Engagement - how long to stand up the Private control plane in their AWS account (us-west-2) + security review? My note earlier said 6-8 weeks; is that still accurate?

Thanks - I can take notes during the security call and share the Q/A pack.
